quotes.text: It is by doing just acts that we become just, by doing temperate acts that we become temperate, by doing courageous acts that we become courageous.
quotes.original: οὕτω δὴ καὶ τὰ μὲν δίκαια πράττοντες δίκαιοι γινόμεθα, τὰ δὲ σώφρονα σώφρονες, τὰ δ᾽ ἀνδρεῖα ἀνδρεῖοι.

source.work: Nicomachean Ethics

quotes.verification_note: Replaces quotes-final q064 (same passage, W. D. Ross 1908 wording 'we become just by doing just acts…'; Ross †1971, so that translation is protected in the EU until 2041). Welldon †1937 (public domain). Greek matched on el.wikisource 'Ηθικά Νικομάχεια/2' (normalised, accents stripped) = True. This is the genuine source of 'We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act but a habit' — Will Durant's 1926 paraphrase (see REJECTED-V2).

quotes.text: For as one swallow or one day does not make a spring, so one day or a short time does not make a fortunate or happy man.

source.work: Letter to Theo van Gogh, Nieuw-Amsterdam (Drenthe), 28 October 1883
source.locator: Letter 336 (1914/1927 numbering; vangoghletters.org no. 400); 1927 ed. vol. II, p. 332

quotes.verification_note: Replaces quotes.json q078 (2009 Van Gogh Museum translation, 'All Rights Reserved'). Checked 2026-10-04: sentence read from the archive.org OCR of the 1927 Constable edition, vol. II (bwb_C0-BNZ-755_2), search-inside leaf 346 = printed p. 332, under letter no. 336. Excerpt: the sentence continues '…will be silenced, but only by working; …'. Jo van Gogh-Bonger's translation (†1925) is public domain. Dutch matched on vangoghletters.org let400 'original_text' = True; capitals 'SCHILDER DAN JUIST' are Van Gogh's own emphasis. Source of the popular 'If you hear a voice within you say "you cannot paint," then by all means paint, and that voice will be silenced.'

quotes.fame_evidence: Van Gogh's most-quoted line on self-doubt (in the paraphrased 'you cannot paint' form); Wikiquote 'Sourced' (letter of 28 Oct 1883). Evidence type: documented most-cited genuine line; anthology listing not checked.

quotes.text: Be alone, that is the secret of invention; be alone, that is when ideas are born.
quotes.author: Nikola Tesla

source.work: Orrin E. Dunlap Jr., 'An Inventor's Seasoned Ideas: Nikola Tesla, Pointing to "Grievous Errors" of the Past…', The New York Times (8 April 1934), p. X9 — interview with Tesla
source.locator: Quote Investigator, 'Be Alone, That Is the Secret of Invention; Be Alone, That Is When Ideas Are Born' (6 October 2021)

quotes.verification_note: Checked 2026-10-04 on the QI article: display wording = True; the citation (1934 April 8, New York Times, Dunlap, Quote Page X9) read from QI's reference list; QI's conclusion credits Tesla with the statement in that 1934 interview. Wikiquote lists it in its sourced 'Quotes' section with the same NYT citation. NYT page itself (paywalled archive) not opened [not re-checked]. Text rights: NYT 1934 / Tesla (short quotation).

image.creator: Napoleon Sarony (c. 1890), New York; postcard in the Nikola Tesla Museum, Belgrade
image.attribution: Napoleon Sarony, c. 1890, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tesla_circa_1890.jpeg)

quotes.fame_evidence: One of Tesla's most-shared lines and the one QI has confirmed (most of his popular 'quotes' are unsourced); Wikiquote sourced section. Evidence type: documented most-cited genuine line (QI / Wikiquote). Not in ODQ/Bartlett's to my knowledge.

quotes.text: Victory awaits him who has everything in order—luck, people call it. Defeat is certain for him who has neglected to take the necessary precautions in time; this is called bad luck.
quotes.original: Seier venter den, som har alt iorden — held kalder man det. Nederlag er en absolut følge for den, som har forsømt at ta de nødvendige forholdsregler i tide — uheld kaldes det.

quotes.text: Difficulties are just things to overcome after all.
quotes.author: Ernest Shackleton

source.work: The Heart of the Antarctic: Being the Story of the British Antarctic Expedition 1907–1909, vol. I (London: William Heinemann)
source.locator: Vol. I, ch. XXII 'On the Great Glacier', p. 321 — diary entry for 11 December 1908, ascending the Beardmore Glacier

quotes.verification_note: Reused from quotes-final x06. Re-checked 2026-10-04 in the archive.org OCR of the 1909 Heinemann vol. I (heartofantarctic01shacuoft): the sentence is there with an OCR line-break hyphen ('over- come'); search-inside puts 'Difficulties are just things' on leaf 585 (the item's page map reads '821', evidently an OCR slip for p. 321, the page recorded by the explorer pass). No comma before 'after all' in the source; often quoted with one.

image.creator: George Charles Beresford (before 1909); restoration by Adam Cuerden; National Library of Norway
image.attribution: George Charles Beresford, before 1909 (restored by Adam Cuerden), public domain, National Library of Norway, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ernest_Shackleton_before_1909.jpg)

quotes.fame_evidence: Shackleton's most-quoted genuine line (his best-known 'quotes' — the 'Men wanted' advertisement, 'Optimism is true moral courage' — are not sourced to him); Wikiquote 'Quotes' section. Evidence type: documented most-cited genuine line.

quotes.text: That's one small step for (a) man; one giant leap for mankind.
quotes.author: Neil Armstrong

source.work: Apollo 11 air-to-ground transmission, as transcribed in the Apollo 11 Lunar Surface Journal (NASA, ed. Eric M. Jones), 'One Small Step'
source.locator: Mission elapsed time 109:24:23, 20 July 1969 (21 July UTC), stepping off the LM footpad

quotes.verification_note: Reused from quotes-final x16. Re-checked 2026-10-04: normalised match on the NASA ALSJ page = True, at timestamp 109:24:23. The '(a)' is the Journal's bracketing — the article is not clearly audible; Armstrong said he intended it. The app may display it without brackets.

image.creator: NASA (photo S69-31741, July 1969)
image.attribution: NASA (photo S69-31741), public domain, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Neil_Armstrong_pose.jpg)

quotes.fame_evidence: Among the most famous sentences ever spoken; in the Oxford Dictionary of Quotations, Bartlett's and the Yale Book of Quotations [anthology listings cited from memory — not re-checked in the books].

quotes.text: Nothing in life is worthwhile unless you take risks.
quotes.author: Denzel Washington

source.work: 'Fall Forward', Commencement Address at the University of Pennsylvania (16 May 2011), published in Almanac vol. 57, no. 34 (24 May 2011)
source.locator: Penn Almanac transcript, 'Commencement Address by Denzel Washington: Fall Forward'

quotes.verification_note: Checked 2026-10-04 against Penn's own published transcript (Almanac; the live site answers 403 to scripts, so read via the Wayback Machine snapshot of 27 Nov 2020, id_ raw copy): normalised match = True; 'May 16, 2011' = True. Excerpt: the transcript's sentence is 'Well, here it is: I've found that nothing in life is worthwhile unless you take risks.' Quote sites usually glue it to 'Fall forward. Every failed experiment is one step closer to success.' — those are separate sentences ~1,000 characters apart (see B23). Text rights: Washington (speech, short quotation).
